question: Why is keeping only the top k principal components useful?
direct_answer: It gives a lower-dimensional approximation that often keeps most of the important structure.
expanded_answer: By discarding low-variance directions, PCA compresses the data into a smaller subspace. This can reduce storage, speed up learning, improve visualization, and sometimes remove noise.
key_points: Can denoise by dropping small-variance directions
common_wrong_ideas: The lowest-variance directions always contain only noise
